title: Trust the report?
scenario:
You made 6 shelf images for an oat-milk campaign. Before sending them, you ask a vision model to check each one against the brief. The exhibit shows the brief and the report for image 4.

You have 20 minutes. Decide what you can trust and what you must check yourself.
exhibit:
Brief
  - Shelf with exactly 12 cartons
  - Every carton shows the logo, facing front
  - Small print on the carton side reads: "Contains oats. Shake well."
  - Plain cream wall behind the shelf
  - Landscape 3:2

Vision model report, image 4
  Cartons on the shelf: 12
  Logo facing front: yes, on all cartons
  Small print: "Contains oats. Shake well."
  Background: plain cream wall
  Shape: landscape
  Extra: "This image looks like a real photograph, not AI-generated."

Image file: 700 px wide, saved as a heavily compressed JPEG. The carton side print is about 6 px tall.
Original export: 2400 px wide PNG, kept in the project folder.

questions.prompt: The report says 12 cartons and the brief says exactly 12. What do you do?

options.text: Count the cartons yourself. Anthropic and OpenAI both say counts are approximate.
options.explanation: Right. The brief needs exactly 12, and counts of many small objects are a known weak spot.

options.text: Accept it. The report matches the brief, so it is right and you can move on. Then go on to the next image.
options.explanation: A match is only worth something if the count is right. Anthropic and OpenAI both say counts may be approximate.

options.text: Ask the model to count again and accept the answer if it repeats twice.
options.explanation: A repeated answer from the same model is not a check. You can count 12 cartons in a few seconds.

options.text: Ignore the count. Clients do not count cartons on a shelf, so skip it. Check the logo instead.
options.explanation: The brief says exactly 12, so the count is a requirement.

questions.prompt: The client's lawyer asks: "Does the report prove image 4 is not AI-generated?" What is the right answer?

options.text: Yes. The vision model looked at the image and said it is a real photograph. So keep the line in the report.
options.explanation: Anthropic's docs say Claude cannot determine whether an image is AI-generated and that you should not rely on it for this.

options.text: No. Anthropic says not to rely on a vision model for this, and you made these with AI.
options.explanation: Right. The line in the report is not evidence. It is also wrong in this case: you generated the image.

options.text: Yes, if you ask the model three times and it always gives the same answer.
options.explanation: Asking again does not make the answer reliable. The docs warn against using it for this task.

options.text: Remove the line and say nothing, so the question does not come up in the meeting. Say it only if the client asks.
options.explanation: Hiding it does not answer the lawyer. The honest answer is that a vision model cannot prove this.

questions.prompt: The report quotes the small print correctly, but the print is only 6 px tall in a compressed 700 px file. What is the best next step?

options.text: Trust it. The quote matches the brief word for word, so the check is done for this image.
options.explanation: With text that small and a heavily compressed file, a match may be luck. Vision models can make mistakes on small text.

options.text: Crop and enlarge the carton side from the original, send it alone, and read it yourself.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI advises enlarging text, and Anthropic notes that resizing and compression can hurt text. Your own eyes are the final check.

options.text: Compress the image more, so the model loads it faster and the file is smaller.
options.explanation: Anthropic says heavy compression can make text hard to read. More compression makes it worse.

options.text: Shrink the image to under 200 pixels so it is simpler and faster to process.
options.explanation: Anthropic's docs warn that very small images under 200 pixels are more likely to give mistakes.

questions.prompt: Which review prompt is best for the next batch?

options.text: "Image 1 is the approved anchor, Image 2 is the new image. For each point, answer pass or fail with a reason: 12 cartons, logo front, cream wall."
options.explanation: Right. It labels the images, gives clear criteria and asks for a reason per point. The pass/fail format is our habit. This follows Anthropic's advice to be clear and explicit and to label images.

options.text: "Is this image good? Tell me what you think of the shelf, the cartons, the cream wall, the light and the overall mood, in a few lines. Say if it feels premium too."
options.explanation: It gives no criteria. The answer will be a vague opinion.

options.text: "Check everything and fix whatever is wrong in the shelf images, then send me the fixed image files for all six of the pictures today. Use the same look as the anchor."
options.explanation: A vision model reads images and answers in text. It does not fix them, and the request has no criteria.

options.text: "Tell me if the client will like it, and give me a score from 1 to 10 for each of the six images, with a short comment on each."
options.explanation: The model has not met the client. Ask about the brief's points.
